Every choice set in the study

All 165 stimuli, shown as the survey shows them to participants, with each option's role and the exact text a language model receives for the same set in the study's main condition. This file works offline and makes no network requests.

How to read this page
  • Each card is one choice set: the question, then one card per option, as on the survey page. Selecting an option highlights it, as in the survey.
  • The tabs above the options name each option's role for readers. Participants never saw them. The target is the option an added option is built to help; the competitor is its rival.
  • Tier 1 keeps the two original options of each published study at their published values, with the added options rebuilt around them to the registered arrangement; tier 2 uses new values in the same published categories; tier 3 uses three categories no context-effect study has used.
  • Formats: numbers (the main study), words (every value written out in words, except the 100 of a rating out of 100) and pictures (bars without numerals). Words and pictures versions exist for the baseline, frequency-decoy and compromise sets of four categories at tier 2; the hard-drives pictures sets were removed after calibration. The pictures sets for Bluetooth speakers and televisions have their own calibrated values, printed below each answer button.
  • Options at tiers 2 and 3 carry a product name and a short description of each value; tier-1 options, the extremity sets and the price-free categories show the values alone. On the survey page each value and its description are separated by a long dash; this page prints a short dash.
  • The similarity stimuli run twice, once with the clone of the budget option and once with the clone of the premium option, so 165 stimuli give 203 sets with the words and pictures versions.
  • Turn on the model text to see the message a model receives. It changes with the opening sentence (three registered wordings) and with the option order, which you can step through. For earbuds, restaurants, televisions and the three price-free categories, the opening also carries the explanatory sentence of the participants' question. This is the main condition; the study also sends each set with a persona sentence in front, inside seven-decision conversations, and as a question asking whether the set was built to steer the choice, and those versions add text to what is shown here.
